Alopecia affects everyone who has it differently. For some people, it's a couple of small patches. For others, it's progressive, unpredictable, and emotionally exhausting in ways that are genuinely hard to describe. Whatever your experience looks like, you deserve real answers — not a brushed-off "we'll see what we can do."

We've worked with many clients with alopecia. Here's what we've actually learned about finding suitable hair restoration options, including hair extensions for alopecia when natural hair and scalp conditions allow.

The Type of Alopecia Matters

Androgenetic alopecia — gradual thinning over the top of the scalp — can be one of the more workable situations for extensions. There's often enough distributed hair to build on, and the results can be significant when the method is appropriate.

Alopecia areata — patchy, circular hair loss associated with an autoimmune response — is more nuanced. We assess the affected areas carefully and avoid placing extensions where the scalp is sensitive or regrowth may be occurring. The goal is to add density where possible while protecting the natural hair and scalp.

Alopecia totalis or universalis — extensive or complete hair loss — is a different conversation. When there's no natural hair available to support extensions, a lace-front wig may be a more suitable option. We offer wig fittings too, and we'll always recommend what best suits your needs, even if it's not extensions.

How We Approach It

For clients who are suitable candidates, hair extensions for alopecia may be an option depending on the pattern of hair loss, the condition of the remaining hair, and scalp sensitivity. Non-surgical hair replacement systems may also be worth discussing because some options are designed to be repositionable and avoid traditional adhesive application.

We assess each client individually and recommend a method based on what their natural hair can safely support. We avoid options that could add unnecessary tension to vulnerable hair, including heavy fusion bonds or methods that create ongoing pulling at the roots.

One More Thing

A lot of our alopecia clients tell us they've felt dismissed or rushed at other salons. We want you to know that won't happen here. We take the time to understand your specific situation, discuss suitable options, and keep these conversations genuinely private.

If you're exploring hair extensions for alopecia or other hair replacement options, come in and let's talk. Book a free consultation at (212) 221-3881 or online — we're glad you found us.
